text:
Alex Chen: ping — getting a spike of OOMs in rtf-inference-east-1, node pool a3-small, several containers crashed. Grafana alert: paged-attn allocator fragmentation + slow KV cache growth. I opened the thread to coordinate live mitigation.

incident-bot: ALERT: [inference-runtime] node-flap detected rtf-node-11 (east-1). 3 container restarts in 1m. Severity: high.

Priya Nair: seeing same, traces show long GC-ish stalls then cudaMalloc failures. Customer-facing retries started around 02:11 UTC.

Jordan Lee: logs from crashed container (tail):
```
2026-03-15T02:11:34.512Z [runtime] ERROR cudaMalloc returned 2 (out of memory)
2026-03-15T02:11:34.513Z [allocator] paged_attn: request pages=2048 seq=512 -> fragmented_free_pages=8
2026-03-15T02:11:34.515Z [kvcache] store.size=27.4GB growth_rate=1.3GB/10m
2026-03-15T02:11:34.516Z [container] exiting with code 137
```

Mei Wang: pasted nvidia-smi and `kubectl describe pod` output into logs channel. GPU mem shows 99% and many small allocations pinned.

Carlos Ruiz: quick customer impact numbers — synthetic: 3 customers >5s latency, 1 customer hitting 12% 503 rate on generate endpoints in region-east. Putting Affected-Customers list in private escalation doc.

Priya Nair: immediate mitigation plan I propose: 1) drain rtf-node-11, 2) enable model-fallback to smaller-quantized variant for routing, 3) trigger KV cache eviction for long-prefixes, 4) apply allocator compaction flag if safe.

Mandy-Oncall: I'm oncall, taking lead. I'll drain the node and scale up a hot spare pool while we triage. Doing `kubectl drain rtf-node-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.

Jordan Lee: before drain, do we have an automated eviction endpoint? We can nudge KV cache eviction: `POST https://admin.internal/inference/kv/evict?prefix=conversation_prefix_long` with auth. Use small batches. Also we have a runtime flag to turn on aggressive compaction: `--paged-attn-compact-threshold=0.2` but that requires process restart.

Alex Chen: start EVict now on low-risk prefixes. I'll run the curl in a loop to pop oldest prefixes.

Carlos Ruiz: customer mitigation: set up temporary rate-limits for heavy customers and enable retry jitter to reduce thundering herd. Pinged customer success to apply compensating measures.

deploy-bot: DEPLOYMENT: routing-config patch applied to route ~20% traffic to fallback-quantized-v2 in east region. Rollout id: r-20260315-evict-fb

Priya Nair: after the routing patch we see reduced per-GPU allocation pressure on two nodes. But one remaining pod still shows fragmentation and slow leak.

Jordan Lee: gathered heap/allocator metrics: fragmentation ratio trending up, free contiguous pages falling. Hypothesis: paged-attn allocator leaking small fragments due to repeated attention page pinning w/o coalescing on rollover. Need compaction algorithm or forced eviction.

Mei Wang: I can enable runtime diagnostic to collect allocator bitmap and page histograms. Adding this before any restarts: `curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/debug/alloc_stats` on the pod. Will post output.

Alex Chen: results of alloc_stats (snip): "hot_pages: 1420, cold_pages: 12, largest_contiguous_free: 4 pages, total_allocated_pages: 16000" — confirms heavy fragmentation.

Mandy-Oncall: node drained successfully. New node provisioned from hot-spare pool. Some pods rescheduled fine; two pods in CrashLoopBackoff on restart.

Jordan Lee: for CrashLoopBackoff pods, stack shows `cudaMalloc` fails during model load. We should reduce prefetchers and disable KV prewarm on restart for those pods. Patch config: `REDWOOD_KV_PREWARM=false` then restart.

Priya Nair: I'm toggling KV prewarm off for the affected deployment: `kubectl set env deployment/rtf-inference REDWOOD_KV_PREWARM=false -n inference` — will restart pods gradually.

Carlos Ruiz: monitoring customer error spikes. After routing to fallback and node drain, 503 rate dropped to 4% but latency still high for heavy customers. Noted as continuing impact.

Mei Wang: compaction attempt: I applied `--paged-attn-compact=true` with config rollout to a single canary pod. The canary crashed on restart (OOM during compaction). Rolling that back. Compaction is too heavy while memory is tight.

Jordan Lee: alternative: incremental eviction of cold KV prefixes + prefer compacting when node has >20% spare contiguous pages. Create a small script to run eviction+sleep loops.

Alex Chen: launched incremental eviction script (small batches, 1 prefix per 30s) against the largest prefixes. Observation: after ~12 minutes the largest_contiguous_free grew from 4 -> 28 pages. Some pods recovered.

Mandy-Oncall: live mitigation summary so far: drained node, routed 20% to fallback, disabled KV prewarm, incremental KV eviction running, rolled back compaction flag. Will keep incremental eviction until fragmentation stabilizes.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity -> high, 02:30 UTC mitigations partially effective. Ongoing: residual pod OOMs and degraded latency for heavy customers.

Priya Nair: action items for short-term: 1) continue incremental eviction until contiguous free >= 64 pages on all nodes, 2) schedule rolling restarts during low traffic window to apply compaction safely, 3) create alert for contiguous_free_pages < 16.

Carlos Ruiz: immediate customer comms: notify impacted customers with ETA and mitigation actions. I've drafted the message and shared to CS.

Jordan Lee: debug note — I collected kernel dmesg from nodes and found sporadic PCIe AER errors on rtf-node-11 before the flap; likely unrelated but worth hardware check. Filed a ticket with infra.

Mandy-Oncall: I'm going to hand off a follow-up to Priya for the next shift. Priya, take it? I'll include commands we ran and the eviction script in runbook.

Priya Nair: taking handoff. I will keep incremental eviction running and monitor contiguous_free_pages and gpu_util. I'll also coordinate with infra for hardware ticket. Planning to start scheduled rolling restarts at 04:10 UTC during lower traffic.

Alex Chen: notes for postmortem: suspected root causes = slow KV cache growth + paged-attn allocator fragmentation + insufficient fallback routing and isolation. Short-term mitigations: eviction, routing fallback, disable prewarm, drain. Long-term mitigations to evaluate: allocator compaction that is incremental and OOM-safe, KV per-tenant quotas, proactive contiguous_free_pages alerting, and model-loading backpressure.

Mandy-Oncall: leaving log and actions in incident runbook. Handoff complete to Priya at 03:05 UTC.

Priya Nair: last check before I go heads-down: customers with >5s latency reduced from 3 -> 1, 503 error rate stabilized at ~2%. I'll keep updates in thread.

Mei Wang: collecting final diagnostic dumps and will upload to the incident artifact store.

incident-bot: INCIDENT TIMELINE recorded.

Priya Nair: (03:30 UTC) follow-up: incremental eviction succeeded on all nodes; contiguous_free_pages > 64 on 9/10 nodes. One node has persistent small contiguous due to long-lived pinned pages; infra will investigate. Marking mitigations as stable for now. Scheduling PM with eng-runtime.

Mandy-Oncall: thanks team — good coordination. Adding action items to postmortem: add eviction endpoint throttles, safe compaction mode, and routing SLO adjustments.

Alex Chen: assigning postmortem lead: Jordan.

Jordan Lee: accepted. Will draft and include timeline, customer impact, and code pointers.

Carlos Ruiz: closing customer comms loop — CS updated customers with interim timeline and mitigation summary.

Priya Nair: handing off to next oncall at 04:15 UTC. Leaving thread open for any late regressions.

Mandy-Oncall: signoff from me, moving incident to monitoring state. :white_check_mark:
